query: Why did hardware incidents spike in the anomaly window?

judge.outcome_variable: is_hardware_incident (hardware incident occurrence, aggregated as the spike in the anomaly window)

per_column.name: is_in_anomaly_window
per_column.rationale: Flags whether a record falls in the anomaly window. This is the temporal stratifier defining the spike period itself, directly named in the query ('in the anomaly window'). It is not a candidate cause of hardware incidents but rather the time-slice over which the outcome is observed.

per_column.name: days_to_anomaly
per_column.rationale: Signed distance in days to the anomaly window. This is a temporal offset/running variable re-expressing the same window construct from the query. It is not a substantive candidate cause of hardware incidents, only a timing coordinate.

per_column.name: is_critical_or_high
per_column.rationale: Priority severity flag. This is a plausible candidate cause whose association with hardware incidents could be attributed (e.g., were spike incidents driven by high-priority tickets). It functions as a candidate treatment/explanatory variable derived from the priority field, not stated in the query.

per_column.name: is_hardware_incident
per_column.rationale: Directly encodes the outcome of interest (hardware vs not), i.e. the thing being explained. Named explicitly in the query.

per_column.name: is_anomaly_hardware
per_column.rationale: Interaction/conjunction of being in the anomaly window AND being a hardware incident. This is a derived indicator of the outcome-within-window (essentially the spike itself), not a confounder. Conditioning on it mixes outcome and window; it is a restatement of the focus, not a common cause.

judge.rationale: The added columns set up a within-window vs outside-window contrast plus an outcome flag, and at most one candidate cause (priority severity). Crucially, no genuine confounder was surfaced: there is no variable that plausibly causes BOTH the candidate treatment (priority) AND the hardware-incident outcome and is not already implied by the query. The remaining columns merely re-encode the anomaly window (named in query), the outcome (named in query), and their conjunction (a collider/restatement of the spike). No common causes such as vendor/hardware model, system/CI age, change or deployment activity, environment, or load were surfaced from the data. Therefore the columns fail the decisive test for causal attribution: they do not supply confounders that must be adjusted to avoid biased attribution, so confounder_quality is 0.
